constraints.note: No per-run brief. Standing constraints applied: 5 topics, 8 clips = 5 full cuts (clips 1-5, by rank) + 3 impact cuts (clips 6-8) for the three topics with a clear peak. Four of the five fulls are scatter-gathered from separate points of the stream. Evaluation replay: no segment ends after 3923 s (latest out-point is 3320.6).

topics.hook_summary: "You got to get into assets now because this might be your last chance." Robots get mass produced, every job gets completely wiped out, "but the good news is you guys are on to crypto and you have a chance."

"If you're doing a hundred dollars a week, ten dollars into ten different plays, it does add up": the 350x with LAB, the 550x last September, a 20 million market cap that pumped to 7 billion, and the one 300x that more than makes up for the one that rugs.

"Pieverse was one that I kept secret throughout pretty much the entire bear market." VC-funded insider token, agent-to-agent payments, "good for multiple billions... much better than LAB, and LAB went to 7 billion."
"TAO isn't competing. It's the arena." NEAR and Render qualify as one subnet under Bittensor, the TAO token itself is not centralized, and "TAO, I think you're going to get many, many multipliers."
"Good things cooking with Kaspa now that we got the KCC-20 protocol live. Now we have Kaspa tokens, officially... because they're on the L1."

clips.title: Get Into Assets Now, This Might Be Your Last Chance

segments.why: Context: "the robotics narrative is going to be insane... for the whole economy and for humanity", mass production of robots, more than cars. Plays SECOND, after the cold-open hook.

COLD OPEN. "You got to get into assets now because this might be your last chance. So many normal things are going to be so cheap that how the hell do you make extra money to invest." Drops the leading "And".

"Quite literally, this month, everybody's saying programming completely wiped out... every software engineer is acknowledging that AI can now produce better code than us." His own profession, so it carries credibility. Starts after the radiology line on purpose.

The run: software engineers, designers, graphic designers, actors, video "completely wiped out", then the robots take electricians and plumbers, the driverless-truck joke, and the payoff: "the good news is you guys are on to crypto and you have a chance", closing on the yacht line ("rather than spend a hundred million on a yacht we'll spend like, I don't know, 50").

"When these guys hit the market, you're talking about electricians, plumbers, everybody completely wiped out."

clips.notes: Strongest topic of the stream and the only evergreen philosophical one: conviction plus a hopeful tribal payoff, no market narration. Emotional core (to confirm by ear) is segment index 3, the repeated "completely wiped out" hammer through to "you have a chance". Assembly is NOT chronological: it opens cold on the "last chance" line (index 1), then steps back to the robotics setup (index 0). Deliberately left out between segments: the entrepreneurial-mind ramble (568-588), the plug for his next video (588-600), the radiology claim (602-613, unverifiable) and the code-review bottleneck aside (630-645). Tighten candidates inside index 3: the "negative job growth in these sectors" stumble (654.6-662.9) and the restarts around 686.6-694.

clips.title: 10 Dollars Into 10 Plays a Week: How We Got a 350x

segments.why: Hook and the wins: "if you're doing a hundred dollars a week, ten dollars into ten different plays, it does add up", some 50x, the 350x with LAB, the 550x last September, "20 million market cap, watch that bad boy pump to 7 billion", then cash out with thousands in dry powder and rotate. Ends before the 500-dollar-bag ramble.
The spread of outcomes: a lot in the hundreds of Xs, a lot in the dozens, a lot at 2x to 7x, and a few that rug.

The answer to the rug: "if the highest performer is a 300x like LAB, it more than makes up for it. One is the 300x, one rugs, but the other eight still give you multipliers, a 5x, a 10x, a 20x." Starts AFTER the ElizaOS aside.
Closer, lands on the 20x echo: "but I thought we were just going to get like a 20x out of LAB. There's no way I thought we'd go over 350x. I had no idea."

review_callouts: NO VERTICAL MASTER (evaluation replay). The word file carries word START times only, so every out-point is the start of the last word plus roughly 0.5 s, held before the next word. Snap every boundary to silence at the tighten step.
Energy is unverified on all eight clips: I worked from text only. Confirm the emotional core named in the notes of each clip by ear before anything is built.
Clip 2: 2134.2-2155.5 (ElizaOS and the lawsuit) sits between segments 2 and 3 and must never be pulled back in when boundaries are adjusted.

Clips 3 and 8: confirm the project name. The transcript says piverse / pyverse; I read it as Pieverse (agent-to-agent payments, x402). Also confirm the market caps he quotes (300 million for Pieverse, the 85 million example, LAB to 7 billion) are still right at posting time.
Clip 3: "insider tokens" is his own label for VC-funded early plays. Check it reads that way on a caption and not as insider trading.

Clip 4: the hook sentence is a chat comment from a viewer that he reads and agrees with. "The founder stepped down out of that org" needs a fact check before it ships. The NEAR / Render line is a comparison, not a put-down, but it does name two other projects: that is a call for Mike.

Clips 1 and 6: "these guys right here" (675.5) and "one of these bad boys, one of these yachts" (720-723) point at the shared screen. Check the vertical layout shows the robots and the yacht at those moments.
Clip 1 leaves out "radiology completely wiped out" (605-609) because it is not accurate as stated. Keep the in-point of segment 3 at 613.45 or later.

This is a thin 65 minute stream, mostly chat replies, chart tours and tangents. Clips 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 are the ones I would stand behind. Clips 4, 5 and 8 are the marginal ones and the first to delete.
